messages:
sarah: Quick report: our async Python client loses the response body when constructing ApiError for 4xx responses. Customers can't surface validation details (422 JSON) in the UI. :confused:

alex: Which HTTP lib are you on? httpx or requests?

sarah: httpx AsyncClient via our wrapper. Minimal snippet: 
```py
resp = await client._post('/chat', json=payload)
if resp.status_code == 422:
    # resp.json() has useful validation info
    raise ApiError.from_response(resp)
```
ApiError ends up with only status_code and str(message). No raw body or parsed json available. The wrapper closes the httpx.Response after reading a stream and we don't persist the body.

maya: That's bad. I remember we intentionally kept ApiError small to avoid memory blowups, but dropping all JSON is too aggressive.

alex: Agreed. Proposal: ApiError should carry optional raw_body (string), json_body (dict as parsed string), and request_id (from x-request-id or x-rid). Keep fields optional to preserve compatibility. Also add truncated flag when we clamp stored bytes (e.g., 64KiB).

sarah: Implementation notes: for async responses do `body_bytes = await response.aread()` then try json.loads(body_bytes) to populate json_body lazily. For sync use response.content. After reading, close response. Limit to 64*1024 bytes and set truncated=True if longer.

maya: Please ensure retry middleware doesn't treat 4xx validation errors as retriable. The retry filter should check status_code < 500. Also capture request_id for telemetry when raising.

alex: On the typing side: update types.pyi so ApiError has attributes: status_code: int, message: str, headers: Dict[str,str], raw_body: Optional[str], json_body: Optional[dict], truncated: bool, request_id: Optional[str]. Add deprecation note if we remove older attributes.

sarah: I'll add tests: one sync test and one async test that spin up a tiny http server returning 422 with JSON body {"errors": [{"loc": ["prompt"], "msg": "too long"}]}, assert ApiError.json_body preserved and .truncated false. Also a test that returns >64KiB body and assert .truncated true and raw_body length == 64KiB.

maya: For UX, consider `ApiError.normalized_errors` property that returns a List[str] extracted from problem+json or legacy error formats. Populate lazily from json_body to avoid extra parse work.

devex-bot: Created issue #4677: "python: retain response body/json in ApiError for async client + add truncated flag + request_id" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4677 :robot_face:

ci-bot: Note: added failing test tests/test_error_body_preserve_async.py::test_422_body_lost against main.

alex: Nice. Also update changelog + migration note: "If you previously parsed ApiError message text, switch to e.json_body or e.normalized_errors for structured data."

sarah: Will open PR with changes to ApiError, types.pyi, tests, and docs. Assigning to myself. Ping me for review. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — once merged, we should patch the changelog and add a small snippet in the Quickstart showing how to handle validation errors in UIs.

sarah: Yep. PR done in a bit.
